utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I won't have any questions for you at this moment. I'm just going read out your summary statement. I will thank you after that and you will then be cross-examined by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I would read statement summary of Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It is very short one. Pasic, Radomir, in relevant period was president of the Crisis Staff in Bosanski Novi municipality. He will testify on overall situation in Bosanski Novi before and after conflict emerged. He will describe situation in the municipality during the first multi-party elections and emerging of conflict between Serbs and Muslims. He will testify on migration of population and reasons for departure of the Muslim population from the municipality. He will explain political relations in the municipality in 1992 and relation between Serb and Muslim politicians and their representatives. Witness will testify on incidents occurred between Serbs and Muslims in this municipality, contacts with UNPROFOR representatives, and activities on UNPROFOR, as well as on existence of paramilitary units and creation of Crisis Staff. He will explain structure, organisation, and activity of Crisis Staff in Bosanski Novi municipality, and he will also testify on Croatian army shelling Bosanski Novi in 1991. And that's the end of statement summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And you said you have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have anymore questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, you've testified in the Karadzic and Krajisnik cases at this Tribunal; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you tell the truth in those testimonies?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor in 2003; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I think that was the year. In any case, it did take place, although I'm not certain about the year. There was an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And did you also tell the truth in that interview, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you mention in paragraph 4 of your statement that in 1990 you became president of the Municipal Board of the Bosanski Novi SDS. The Novi SDS was founded in late July of 1990; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: It was the initiating committee that was formed in July, and the rest followed in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say "an initiating committee," you're referring to a meeting of 50 to 100 people; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Approximately. It took place in different locations in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you a little bit, Mr. Traldi. You're referring the witness to paragraph 4 of his statement. Is that the statement he gave to the Prosecution or the statement he gave in court here, this one that we've just admitted? I'm looking at paragraph 4 of the statement that we have. It doesn't seem to talk about what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I'd said was that he mentioned in paragraph 4 that he held the post of president of the Municipal Board, and I do see that at the end of paragraph 4. And what I was inquiring was about related topics, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies. I didn't see the second paragraph, the little paragraph. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have another clarification. You referred, Mr. Traldi, you referred to late July 1990. In the response, the witness said August 1991. Which year is correct, 1990 or 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. The multi-party system in the former Yugoslavia came into being in 1990. Perhaps there was a mistake. In any case, there were elections in 1990. It's a matter of general knowledge in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Of course, I couldn't lie about that even if I wanted to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not a question of lie but correctness of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just so we have it completely clear, sir, was it your evidence that this initiative committee was formed in late July 1990, then the actual founding session of the Bosanski Novi SDS took place in August of 1990, is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Velibor Ostojic from the republican-level SDS leadership attended the founding session; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Municipal Board of the Bosanski Novi SDS was implementing the goals and the politics of the republican-level leadership of the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: We implemented the policy according to the statute of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so is that, yes, you implemented the goals and the policy of the republican-level leadership in Bosanski Novi; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't mean that. Someone can order something willfully but we wouldn't implement it if it was not in keeping with the statute of the SDS. There is an enormous difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look just briefly at a portion of your OTP interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31937 and page 14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now towards the bottom of the page in the English, we see you're asked: "Is it fair to say that the policies and goals of the republic-level SDS leaders were the same policies and goals at the Bosanski Novi municipal SDS level?" And you answered: "Yes, of course, it's a normal thing, because the municipal level, the Municipal Board was actually implementing the, the goals and politics of the repub ... of the higher level." Now, do you stand by the truthfulness of that answer that you gave in your OTP interview in 2003?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it was translated correctly, especially in view of the fact that I cannot read the English language. If you understand my previous answer, the sense of it runs counter to what we can read here. I repeat: Policy was being implemented according to the statute of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask a question, sir: Who set out the policy of the SDS at the republican level? Or let me remove "at the republican level." Who set out the policy of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were party organs, party bodies, that were in charge of policy. I understood the gentleman to ask me about some individuals in the party, such as those in leadership functions. In any case, the party had its Main Board, there was an Assembly of the SDS, and the Presidency of the party. Those are the bodies of the party that were supposed to create policy, to repeat, in keeping with the statute of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that -- those assemblies were at the republican level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were some on the municipal level as well, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Bosanski Novi SDS followed, didn't it, the policy that was set out by the party organs and party bodies you just described?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think there were any deviations or failures to implement the chartered policy at that time. For the most part, the party organs were honoured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Bosanski Novi had a representative on the SDS Main Board named Mile Grbic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I know he was in some period, but I can't tell you the dates between which he was a member of the Main Board. He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, when he served on the Main Board, one of his responsibilities was to come back to Novi and inform the SDS there of what had been decided at the Main Board; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: He lived in Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. He would attend meetings of the Main Board elsewhere; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Probably. I can't be sure whether he attended all the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you're quite sure he attended some of them, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about anything, but I suppose he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we can have page 50 of the same interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're asked at the top about Mr. Grbic, and you confirmed he was a member of the Main Board. And then you were asked: "Now, certainly a member of the Main Board of the SDS is going to come back and report to their various municipalities, to the SDS officials, about what happened at the meetings? " And you answered: "Yes, they would definitely transmit the live information that was on the agenda and they would inform us of ..." And then you were asked: "And it makes perfect sense in that there's only 57 deputies on the Main Board that their responsibility then is to go back to their municipalities and form, inform the rest of the SDS members about what happened." And you replied: "Mostly it was so, although there were instances when some -- when sometimes some presidents of the Municipal Boards would attend in addition to the members of the Main Staff," which I take to reflect Main Board, "not all of them, not always, but sometimes that was up to the assessment of the necessity." Do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of that answer that you gave in your OTP interview, as I've just read it out to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I said any different now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the record, it's important that you answer yes or no. Do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of the answers from your interview that I've just read back to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know what this quotation is about. Is there a question, or are you just noting something or making a statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, the question was, and this is the third time I've asked it now, whether what you said in your OTP interview that I quoted to you just now was truthful, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And moving on from that topic, then, you mention you were president of the Municipal Assembly in Bosanski Novi and president of the Bosanski Novi Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, in one time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the time-period covered by your evidence in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the chairman of the Executive Committee in Bosanski Novi during that same period was also a SDS member, Nikola Omazic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Nikola Omazic, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, before we turn into detail to events in Bosanski Novi in 1992, I want to see if we agree on two points, and I'm going to ask you to answer simply yes, you agree, or no, you don't. First, are we in agreement that many thousands of Muslims left Bosanski Novi during the war, including in the period May through July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, one part of the Muslim population left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, second, you refer to the damage or destruction of certain mosques in Bosanski Novi in your statement. Are we agreed that all the mosques in Bosanski Novi were either seriously damaged or destroyed during the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, they were damaged. To what extent the damage was to the construction, I don't know, but they were damaged. Churches were damaged too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we're agreed that's all of them that were damaged or destroyed, even if you're not certain of the extent of the damage to each specific one; right? All of the mosques.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I think so, but I can't be sure. There were mosques in various locations. The mosques that were located in towns were damaged. For the rest, in the rural areas, I don't know that they were completely destroyed or seriously damaged. But they were damaged. It's difficult to assess to what extent. Just as the churches were damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now -- and in this regard, you say in paragraph 43 of your statement that the mosques were set on fire - the mosques described there - by unknown perpetrators. Is it right that you don't yourself know who caused the damage or destruction of those mosques?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't know. We had a great problem, as I emphasised in my testimony and in my statement, with paramilitary groups and individual paramilitaries, and we suspected that it was them who committed these crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, that's just a suspicion, of course, because you don't know the identities of the perpetrators yourself in your evidence; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I believe that's what I said in my written statement, that in most of the cases of damage done to public and private property, no action was taken by municipal or other authorities, and there was even no discussion about it, from which it follows that these cases of destruction and damage in Bosanski Novi were created were the responsibility, mainly, of these paramilitary formations, and I don't know exactly where these paramilitary groups came from, and I stand by that. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. But if you can listen again to the question. The question was not whether or not it was this military -- paramilitaries who did it. The question was it's only a suspicion on your part that those were the perpetrators because you yourself don't have any knowledge. You would help just by just saying "yes" or you say "no" or "I don't know." Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, turning now to a slightly different topic and the lead-up to the conflict. In paragraph 7 of your statement, you assert that Muslims were preparing for war. Now, the Bosanski Novi TO under the command of Mile Damjanovic was also acquiring additional weaponry in early 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Damjanovic was the TO Staff commander and the TO Staff was a legal institution and he worked within his remit. As to how he obtained weapons, I don't think he needed to procure weapons because the system of Yugoslavia at that time was that there were arsenals of weaponry in the municipalities --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: -- under the control of Territorial Defence units and those weapons were light infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- I'm going to stop you there. I understand that your answer is that you don't recall the Territorial Defence having acquired additional weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution have 65 ter 18367.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as it comes up, Mr. Damjanovic, the TO commander, was a member of your Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you did not properly qualify my previous answer. May I respond? I only said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no need. You've just given your answer. That's fine. Can we go on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. Although, we don't have the right document, which I imagine may be an error in my notes. Do we have 65 ter 18367?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is the document I was looking for. This is a request from the Bosanski Novi Territorial Defence Municipal Staff dated the 16th of March, 1992, for the distribution and issue of material supplies. And we see, for instance, several hundred rifles of various sorts. Looking down at points 15 through 17, approximately half a million bullets of different types. So this, in fact, is an example of the Bosanski Novi TO seeking to procure additional weaponry in March 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Considering the job I was doing, it was not my responsibility, so I can't either deny or confirm this. If it's an original document we're looking at, then you're probably right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Who was it sent to? I don't know. Was it sent to me or someone else?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It reflects it was sent to Military Post 1754 in Petrovac, as I read it.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I have nothing to do with this. And considering my post, I wasn't even supposed to know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: How often did you meet with Mr. Damjanovic in April and May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: It's impossible to answer now after so much time. We did meet, but I could easily make a mistake if I told you it was two, five, ten times. But we did meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can analyse it a little bit together. How often did your Crisis Staff meet?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you even that now. There were moments when the Crisis Staff, depending on the situation, convened all day long, and there were other times when we met two or three times a day, and there were also periods when we didn't meet at all for 10 or 15 days. It all depended on the current situation and the tensions. We held meetings as life dictated necessities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I appreciate it's hard to recall the frequency after this amount of time. Would it be right to say your recollection was fresher when you were interviewed by the OTP and when you testified in the Krajisnik case, both about ten years ago, than your recollection is today?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I think only doctors could say whether I am or am not losing my mind. I don't think either of us is really qualified to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was not the question, sir. The question never said you're losing your mind. The question said you may have forgotten because of passage of time. So I would ask you to -- not to try to ridicule the lawyer, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to insist on an answer to my original question. Your recollection of events in 1992 was fresher in 2003 and in 2005 than it is today. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I must say that I did not ridicule you. Second, it is only logical that you remember things better when they are recent, and with the passage of time memories fade. Now I really can't say whether I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is so difficult than in answering the question very simply: Yes, it was fresher then than it is now. Just answer that, then, if you know that it is logical. Why do you go round and round and not just telling, yes, sir, I remembered things better then than I do now because time has passed. That's what I mean by you're trying to ridicule him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't going round and round and I wasn't mocking anyone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Answer the question, then. If you're not going round and round, answer the question now. You remember things better then than you do now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I answered. Should I say any more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In that respect, sir, I'd like to call up a page of your Krajisnik testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 31933, page 138.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you'd been asked about arming of Serbs in Bosanski Novi, there'd been some back and forth about it. And you were asked here, beginning at line 8: "Are you -- the sources of weapons for the Serbs in your community prior to the beginning of the war, what were the sources? " And at that time, when your recollection was fresher, you responded: "Well, of course, those weapons had come from military units, in several different ways." First, what you recalled in 2005 is the truth; right? Serbs in Bosanski Novi, including the TO, received weapons from military units.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: To some extent, yes. Although I don't remember whether I said this at that time. However, I have to emphasise that Novi Grad is on the border with the current Republic of Croatia, and the conflict had broken out one year earlier. So there were many ways to illegally obtain weapons through these channels. And it was the same with the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the document we just saw, however, is an example of the Serbs, in that case, the Serb TO commanded by a member of your Crisis Staff, getting weapons or requesting weapons from the military, just like you described in your Krajisnik testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly. But your previous question was not exactly the same. You said "the Serbs." When you said the Serbs, I didn't understand that as military formations. The Territorial Defence is a military formation, whereas when you say "the Serbs," it could mean civilians too. So we are talking about two different parties, two different sides in this question of supply of weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we stop you there, sir. Can we stop you. You're not -- you are referring to a previous question. Could you please answer the current question and forget about the previous question, because you didn't comment on that when it was asked at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you then please repeat the current question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. The document we just saw is an example of the Serbs - in that case, the Serb TO - getting weapons from military units, just like you described in your Krajisnik testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Because you seem to put an equality mark between Serbs and Territorial Defence. The Territorial Defence probably requested weapons along legal channels; whereas, the Serbs could obtain weapons by different means, including illegal ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's take that one at a time. First, it's right that the Serb Territorial Defence was receiving weapons from military units; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No, not the Serb Territorial Defence. In Bosnia-Herzegovina as it was then, it was still the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you. I'm not speaking legally. But as of March 1992, the TO in Bosanski Novi was commanded by a Serb who became a member of your Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there were Muslims on it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to -- at this time, I have to object. In the question was Serb --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- Territorial Defence, Your Honours. Serb Territorial Defence. First, it should be established whether there was a Serb Territorial Defence in Novi Grad in March 1992 or is there any misunderstanding. But please, it has to be very clear at what point of time it became Serb Territorial Defence and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we see the document again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. Though, to briefly respond: First, I think I was in the process of doing that a moment ago. Second, that's the type of objection that we've asked be made with the witness's headphones off several times, I think, even in the last couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct. But Judge Fluegge is asking that we see the document again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 18367.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, while it's up --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- by this point in March 1992, after the mobilisations in the fall of 1991, the personnel in the Territorial Defence, the great majority were Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: It was proportionate to the population. Bosanski Novi was a majority Serb place, and in the former Yugoslavia, great attention was paid to proportional representation, so the Crisis Staff had a proportionate number of Muslim representatives. The number of Croats in Novi Grad was negligible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, it was translated "Crisis Staff" and this gentleman is talking about TO Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Lukic. You started talking without me having given you an opportunity to talk and I didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was translated "Crisis Staff" and this gentleman is talking about TO Staff, so Territorial Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Well, then it's corrected accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, in your submission, when people were mobilised in Bosanski Novi in the fall of 1991, equal percentages of Serbs and Muslims responded to the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have distinguish -- can this gentleman take off his headphones. I don't want to be inappropriately [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, could you take off your headphones. Do we know that Mr. Pasic doesn't understand English? I know he referred slightly to this sometime back a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can ask in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have to make distinction in between mobilisation and TO members. Mobilisation was for JNA. TO was in connection with municipalities. And -- so I -- I don't want my colleague to mix mobilisation of JNA units with TO Staff in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before even Mr. Traldi answers the question. You know, that a wrong question is being asked is no ground for objection. Because if a wrong question is asked, on re-examination you have the opportunity to say, Sir, you were asked about a Crisis Staff but were you talking about a Crisis Staff or were you talking about the Territorial Defence? Then you correct the record at that. An objectionable question has nothing to do with a question that is incorrect. The Prosecutor was just asking a question. And the witness could answer and say, No, I know nothing about Crisis Staff, and I know something about the TO, if he recognises that the question is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, we have the document regarding TO in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I accept that. I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if he makes a mistake or -- then you can correct that mistake in re-examination. It is not a ground for objection. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Separate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now Mr. Pasic should put his headphones back on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, let me do this in two steps and try to do it very clearly. First, when there was mobilisation into JNA units in Bosanski Novi in the fall of 1991, proportionally -- or an as percentage of the population, more Serbs responded than Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Everyone was being called to respond to the mobilisation, but Muslims, at least most of them, did refuse that call.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Separately, then, or similarly, by March 1992, more Serbs were participating in the Bosanski Novi TO commanded, again, by a member of your Crisis Staff, than Muslims. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's logical. According to the percentages of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind me, is it 18367 or 31933. 183.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 183. Thank you so much. It is admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar, could you please give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 18367 receives exhibit number P7099, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to move ahead in time a little bit now, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can the Prosecution have 65 ter 07996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, in your statement you mention a time when you say you told Charles Kirudja that it was impossible to ensure the safety of Muslims in Bosanski Novi. Now, that was a message you also delivered to the Muslims of Bosanski Novi; right? That you couldn't guarantee their safety.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: The entire population of Novi Grad municipality, they were all subject to us not being able to guarantee their security.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, we're looking here at a document coming from the Crisis Staff on the 8th of June, 1992. It's -- it's identified as going to the citizens of Blagaj and the Japra valley. Those are Muslim areas; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: There was a proportion of the Serbian population there as well, although they were in the minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we're going to go through the events in a moment. In fact, sir, by this time, the 8th of June, thousands of Muslims had been pushed into Blagaj from villages in and around the Japra valley. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No. If I understood the proper interpretation, you said they were pushed into, but I would say moved. I don't know whether it was poor interpretation, but it certainly didn't develop along those lines. I object to the word "pushed into."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this document, this document in the first paragraph says: "On 7 June 1992 you were informed by the Bosanski Novi Red Cross organisation about the problems of departure of Muslims from the territory ..." So the message that's being sent here relates to the departure of Muslims specifically, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: That's different. The previous question was interpreted in quite another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please answer this question and forget about the previous question. You've commented on the previous question. This document was addressed to Muslims, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would first need to see the document. Could we please zoom in because it is unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Can you zoom in the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit more, please, if possible. I can't make anything out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is quite illegible. I really can't see. Can we perhaps look at the signature block to see whether the document is authentic? Can it be scrolled down?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I think you -- you asked for enlargement of the first paragraph. Can it be enlarged a bit further. It's not about authenticity at the moment but about the content. Can you read it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am trying to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to be very specific, in the both first and the second paragraphs, it refers directly to Muslims, and you can read the word "Muslimanske," the first word in the third line in the first paragraph, and the second word in the third line -- sorry, the first word in the third line of the first paragraph; second word, third line, second paragraph. Right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to find it. I see that it says here the existing terrorist groups of ethnic makeup. I see that in the second paragraph. I'm looking for another instances of the word "Muslim" being referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you've just, in fact, declined to read the word "Muslim" that comes after the words "terrorist groups," haven't you? You see the word "Muslim" right there.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Please help me. It is very illegible. It is not that I'm trying to avoid answering, but I really can't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could just show the witness the word "Muslimanske" in the third line of the second paragraph, if you can go to his screen, please. It is so visible and legible to anybody who even doesn't know the language.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the current level of enlargement, do you also see the same word at the beginning of the third line of the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: The second paragraph: "Groups of Muslim ethnicity." Is that it? Groups of ethnic -- Muslim ethnicity, the second paragraph, second or third -- third line. I see "groups of Muslim ethnicity." Is that it? The second paragraph, third line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's one of them. Now look at the first paragraph --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Look at the first paragraph and look at the beginning of the third line.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, Muslim. I think the word ends with an O. However, in terms of the whole sentence, I'm still unable to decipher its meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, we'll look at it in a little bit more detail in a moment. But first, there's a document coming from the Crisis Staff. And so this is -- regardless of who signed it, this is your document; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have to zoom out a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't say it was the case. I see in the title now that it was a notification sent to the inhabitants of Blagaj and Japra valley. So the inhabitants, not Muslims. Perhaps we can scroll back down to see the title. Let me repeat: Based on this document, and I suppose it is accurate in terms of what I could see at the top in block letters -- in any case, it says: "To the inhabitants of Blagaj and Japra valley."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, can we stop you please. Again, I must ask you to please listen to the questions. We're not asking you to explain what the title is. The question really was: But this is a document coming from the Crisis Staff, and so this is - regardless of who signed it - this is your document; right? Is it your document or is it not your document? Answer that question. That's the question put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Perhaps but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you look at the person who is written to have -- who is supposed to have signed the document. Just look at the end of the document. Can you read that or is it also too illegible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is for that reason -- well, if we look at the signature block, it says president of the Crisis Staff, Radomir Pasic. But I think the word "for" is written in with a pen. I really can't say from this point, so much time later, that -- whether it's accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, I don't see the word "for." You have just been saying you don't see words here. Can we scroll it up a little bit, please. Up -- no, down, I'm sorry, down. I'm sorry. Right. If I see what looks like the signature, it looks like what I saw on your statement today. Something that looks like, appears.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, if you look at just above the typed word "Radomir," on the left-hand side, I think it is in the Latin script, and the word is "for" or "za." That is one possibility. Another possibility is that it was scanned --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I can't deny --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: -- or confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can I just stop --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can -- yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you and I'm going to ask you two brief follow-up questions. First, if it's signed for you, that means someone is signing on your behalf and the document is going out under the Crisis Staff's authority; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: If that is the case, then yes. On behalf of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, and related to whether you were communicating that you were unable to guarantee security to everyone or to just Muslims, can you read out, since we only have the B/C/S on our screens, the very last sentence of this document, starting with the word "ukohilko."

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Please enlarge a little bit more. "Should these proposals be rejected, the Crisis Staff will no longer be able to...," I think it should be "to guarantee," "... the safety of Muslim citizens in that area."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note we're around the time for the break. I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 07996 receives Exhibit P7100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. In fact, you are right, Mr. Traldi. We have gone past the time. We take a break. Will you please follow the usher, sir. Again, we'll call you in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, how much time do you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I'll be the rest of the day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, should we perhaps excuse the next witness, if he's here?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we didn't call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You didn't call him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, all right. Thank you so much. That's much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because I -- I was checking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can the witness please be brought into court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So regarding the document that we'd looked at immediately before the break, sir, that was a declaration that -- advising the Muslims in this area that the Crisis Staff was prepared to provide a peaceful and secure departure and noting that it would not be able to guarantee security for the Muslims if they did not accept that proposal. Now, your Crisis Staff never made an announcement inviting Serbs in the area to leave their homes, did it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: If we take it the way you put it, I don't think there were any such announcements. But in terms of guaranteeing safety to anyone, I don't think it was guaranteed to anyone, including Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But aside from not explicitly guaranteeing their safety, you also didn't invite them to leave, did you? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. Did you ever make an announcement: Please leave your homes, Serbian villagers?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I think there were some similar situations when safety could not be guaranteed to the Serbs and when they left their homes as well. I think there were such cases during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I hail from Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to cut you off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 31934, page 28. And this will be another part of your testimony in the Krajisnik case when your recollection of these events was fresher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: While this comes up, I would like to ask the witness, sir, Mr. Pasic, you were talking about, again, in answering the question about guarantee of safety. But that was not the question. The question was if any Serbs were invited by announcement of the Crisis Staff to leave their homes in your municipality. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was my understanding as well, but I didn't understand the time-period it referred to. I responded by saying that there were such moments in time when the Serbs had to leave their homes as well and their safety was not guaranteed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, the question was about an announcement. Was there an announcement, an invitation to the Serbs to leave their homes? Please answer that question, not another one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't want to imagine things, but I'm just saying that there were situations when, by way of radio or a written document or any other type of communication, such things did happen. Of course, to a lesser extent, but they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Were there announcements by the Crisis Staff ordering or inviting Serbs to leave their homes? You should know that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If you understand me, my answer is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I don't understand you. Your answer is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me try to explain, to be precise and accurate. If we take a specific period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, please. It's a very simple question, which was now put several times to you. Do you know of any announcements that Serbs should leave their homes in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat. There were moments when nobody could have their safety guaranteed in certain locations. There were such instances. Not only to the Muslims but to the Serbs as well. Even the Serbs could not have their safety guaranteed at specific periods of time and at specific locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I state that you are not answering the question, that you're not willing to answer the question, and this is a serious problem because you are here to answer questions to the best of your knowledge, to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I'm not talking about the guarantee given to anybody. I'm talking about the announcement that Serbs should leave. Do you know of any such case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if you understood me well and whether you like my answer or not. Let me reiterate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were moments when the Serbs had to leave their areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, stop. Mr. Traldi, please continue. You're not answering my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I've called up this page of transcript because you did answer this question in the Krajisnik case. You were asked first: "My question, Mr. Pasic, was were the Serb villagers in the Japra valley asked to leave their villages and go to another location where they would be more secure? Yes or no." And at first you said: "I can't answer with a yes or no because there was displacement from Serb houses as well, but not pursuant to a command." And then Judge Orie asked you: "Mr. Pasic, again, the question was not whether any Serbian families would have left their homes but whether they were asked to leave their villages and go to another location. That was the question. Did you ever make an announcement: Please leave your homes, Serbian villagers?" And you responded: "Well, I said that as far as I know, that didn't happen, but people did leave their houses for security reasons." Now I have a simple yes-or-no question for you: Do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of your Krajisnik testimony on this point, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 08010.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an announcement from the Red Cross of Bosanski Novi municipality, the 7th of June, the day before your announcement. Now, looking at the second paragraph, they're also relaying that the Crisis Staff is not in a position to guarantee the Muslims safety and discussing the Muslims moving away specifically; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Again, I can't read this, but what you said is true, safety could not be guaranteed at that time to the Muslim population in the area of the Japra valley where the Muslim population was in the majority. There were some Serbs there as well, and they, too, could not have their safety guaranteed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 08010 receives Exhibit P7101, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, a few weeks earlier there were operations that you referred to in paragraph 12 of your statement, mixed patrols of the civilian police, military police, and TO searched the villages of Suhaca, Hozici, Japra, Crna Rijeka, Blagaj, and Agici between the 15th and 20th of May, 1992. Those were all Muslim villages; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: 90 per cent Muslim. Maybe more. There was the odd Serbian house as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 08032.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as it comes up, the special unit of the Banja Luka CSB also participated in those operations; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: It is possible that was the case. I can't say anything exactly. I think there were certain formations at the time of the then-army, and, of course, the civilian police, but I can't recall exactly with any reliability who was included. It is possible that the unit you referred to was included.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, this is a document dated the 21st of May, 1992, coming from the Bosanski Novi SJB, and it's a report on the work and actions by a unit from the special purposes detachment in the area under the control of this SJB and it's being sent to the Banja Luka CSB. So it says in the first paragraph that: "On 11 May 1992 ... uncontrolled shooting erupted first in the town and then around the predominantly Muslim villages in the Japra valley and the Security Services centre of Banja Luka dispatched a unit from the special purposes detachment under the command of Mirko Lukic and a military police unit under the command of Major Stupar ..." And we see below that, in the second paragraph, that the Bosanski Novi SJB sent this special unit to search the Muslim part of Bosanska Kostajnica. And in the third paragraph, that a large number of citizens complained to the Bosanska Kostajnica police station that this special unit was entering houses by force, beating up the men, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to the end of the document in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This report comes from Dragomir Kutlija, the SJB chief. He was also a member of your Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the Crisis Staff, as per his function.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at the time does this reflect your -- or does this refresh your recollection that at the time, in fact, you would have been aware that the special unit of the Banja Luka CSB was involved in these operations and mistreating Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: This is a different period that you are referring to. It is the area of Kostajnica. It is true that some units, or perhaps the unit with that name, was active in the area of Kostajnica. There, we could observe that they were not acting in keeping with the then-regulations and laws. At one of the sessions of the Crisis Staff, we asked Mr. Dragomir Kutlija, the chief, to react, in order to establish law and order and protect the people there who, according to our information, were being mistreated in different ways. As a municipal body, we demanded that unlawful activities be stopped. As far as I recall --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: -- I think our request was met.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll tender it. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you go on. The record didn't record complete the record what I said earlier about P7101. I did say it is admitted into evidence, may it please be given an exhibit number. If the record could just show that clearly. Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Traldi. You wanted to tendered something.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was going to ask for another exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, I say it: 08032 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit P7102, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, ma'am. Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 08036.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a report of the Bosanski Novi Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report of the Bosanski Novi Crisis Staff that was sent to the municipal assembly. Now, first, I've reviewed your past testimonies carefully. Am I right that in your evidence this report is genuine and you believe it was prepared by the secretary of the Municipal Assembly, a man named Djordje Pravuljac.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I would have to read this document before saying whether it's authentic. I can't see these small letters. But if I could read it, I would probably be able to remember. The secretary was indeed Djordje Pravuljac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, just to save time let's call up 65 ter 31933, page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be another portion of your sworn testimony in the Krajisnik case, and that was after you had read through this report. So at the top of the this page, asked by Mr. Krajisnik's counsel, you testified: "I said yesterday evening that this report was written. I didn't personally draft it. It was an assessment, I think. On one page of the report, it says that the person was the secretary of the municipal assembly of Novi Grad. Let me just find the page. His name is Djordje Pravuljac. I think he actually drafted the report because he was in charge of information and some kind of propaganda." Do you stand by that portion of your Krajisnik testimony regarding this report as accurate and truthful, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I've already said, I stand by my entire testimony in both Karadzic and Krajisnik. I stand by both the reports. Maybe I put it a little differently this time, but the meaning is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so it's correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, in fairness to the witness, I don't see any reference in the -- what you quoted from the Krajisnik case in -- reference to the fact that this document is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He said this report was written, I didn't draft it, and this is who I think I drafted it, which is how I'd -- which I'd understood to confirm that this has been draft -- this had been drafted and he was able to identify the drafter. But the witness having stood by his Krajisnik testimony, in that respect I think he's confirmed what I have asked him to confirm, at least, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. If you are satisfied from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this report was submitted to and accepted by the Municipal Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I have a feeling that we are playing with words here. If I understood the interpretation correctly, now you said something different from what we discussed before --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: -- please do not be ambiguous and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, please don't come and conduct classes on how questions must be asked. The lawyer asks you questions and you answer his question as he puts it. He puts it that way because he wants to put it that way. It's not for you to decide for him what kind of question to put to you, okay? Just answer the question as it is put to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I understand you're a lawyer by training yourself and you may have asked questions at times, and I'd just ask that you respect what may be our stylistic differences in how we put them. And separately I'd ask that you answer the question I'd asked a moment ago. The report we looked at on the work of the Crisis Staff was submitted to the Municipal Assembly and accepted by them; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Let's have page 133 of this same document. And I'm looking for the bottom of the page. Very bottom. And you're asked: "This report that was signed by you and submitted to the municipal assembly ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "... was accepted by the municipal assembly with the assertions that are contained in it; correct?" And you answered: "Yes, it was accepted. That is clear enough if you look at the conclusions that we've reviewed." Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if we are talking about the same document then, because obviously my colleague is now mentioning something that was discussed in another trial that was signed. I don't see that this document is signed. At least I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, if we look at -- sorry, there are several points in the document that correspond to what's being discussed. But if we flip back to the previous page, this refers to a report on the Crisis Staff. This is the same document. It's discussed for a while. He says -- the witness says: "This is not my personal report. It's a report produced by the Crisis Staff." And so we're not putting to him that he'd signed it himself. But -- or I'm not putting to him that he'd signed it himself, just that the transcript reflects the same document. But if it it's more efficient, the witness having affirmed his previous testimonies in their entirety, I can simply go through the transcript with Mr. Lukic after the session today, and if we agree that they're talking about the same document, agree that he's affirmed that principle in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I cannot cure this, since obviously in another trial something signed was mentioned. I cannot cure and make something unsigned to be signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think we've used time -- we've used a great deal of time today, and the solution of looking at the transcript together is efficient for the use of court time. But I do think if we look at the transcript together in detail, it will certainly be clear whether it's the same document or not. And I'd suggest we do that after this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But also today it was proposed to the witness that he confirmed something signed, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm willing to withdraw that question for the moment pending my discussion with Mr. Lukic after the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is withdrawn. You do it -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The question only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question is withdrawn. Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have back 65 ter 08036. And if we could have page 8 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read -- and it's two paragraphs below the number 3. Well, the first paragraph below it we read a discussion about stands and political decisions on voluntary relocation and the forming of a working group thereon. And below that, we read: "Before this action started to be carried out more seriously, problems arose in the valley of Japra. The regional staff of TO Agic, Rujinka, and Krsalj, that is, members of their units, turned a deaf ear to endeavours of the official politics and organs of the authorities and started to solve things on their own. Armed activities, which included use of mortars, caused expulsion of Muslim civilians from the villages of G. Agic, Celopek, Hozic, Suhaca, and they were taken to the settlement of Blagaj." Now that's the truth as to how Muslims got -- the Muslims who had been gathered in Blagaj at the time of your warning got there, that their villages had been attacked with mortars that had caused their expulsion and they were taken to Blagaj; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I do remember the details and I remember that part of that District Staff in that area, Velika Rujiska, in Mala Novska Rujiska, some of these people did not listen to the warnings of the command and did something that, in our eyes, wasn't lawful. What happened was fire was opened from mortars and the Muslim population, probably in fear, moved at that time towards Blagaj village which was also Muslim. Very quickly these people were disqualified, they no longer worked in the District Staff, so the staff put an end to it. The Crisis Staff, if I remember correctly, put an end to this. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: -- it's precisely for this reason, if can I see well from this report, that action was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, you testified earlier that as a matter of your position you didn't have involvement with the TO when we were talking about arming. Now you assert that the Crisis Staff dismissed members of the Territorial Defence District Staff. Those are contradictory answers both of which tend to insulate you from the preparations for the conflict and the crimes committed during it. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No, you didn't understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to object, anyways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My colleague is comparing arming and personal involvement of this gentleman into issues of employment; who would be employed with TO. So arming is one thing, and employment into TO is another thing. So it cannot be contradicting, as I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you -- can ... just keep quiet please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to respond -- No, no. It's not for you. It's for the current lawyer to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think it's a fair question, and I admit I don't fully understand the grounds for the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can clarify my objection if you want, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, we've heard your objection. Let's just read what you -- the question you asked, Mr. Traldi. Now, I'm sorry, I'm not finding it very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 84, line 8 and further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 84 and line 8 and further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. "First, you testified earlier that as a matter of your position you didn't have involvement with the TO when we were talking about arming." He didn't have involvement. Now you assert that the Crisis Staff dismissed members of the Territorial Defence District Staff. If you say -- the topic was arming but the answer was I'm not involved with the TO. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: TO arming. If you decide on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- membership was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- can we look at the sentence, please. A moment ago you testified that as a matter of your position you did not have involvement with the TO. At the time when you said you didn't have involvement with the TO, we were discussing arming. So it is involvement with the TO. Now, dismissing the TO is involvement with the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Personally but not in arming-wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. Can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll re-ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection has been overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, earlier you testified, when we were discussing arming, that you had no involvement with the TO. Now you're testifying that the Crisis Staff could dismiss members of the Territorial Defence. These are contradictory answers, both of which tend to insulate you from what the Territorial Defence was doing; first, in preparations; and second, in committing crimes in Bosanski Novi. Right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No, no, that's not correct. You're asking me for short answers and that leads to confusion. I didn't say that the Crisis Staff replaced these people. What happened is we asked the Territorial Defence to take steps in those external District Staffs and not to allow unlawful actions. So the essence is completely different. I continue to maintain that we had no authority to issue any commands or orders along the military chain of command, but we did exert our influence and at that time, and I can't remember whether it was in writing or verbally, we did ask that law and order be restored to what was then the municipality of Novi Grad. So it was not me personally or my intention or my request: Look, go and replace this and that person. No. We addressed the TO requesting that they take steps to put a stop to illegal acts. That was within our purview and that was the limit of our activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we look at the document on the screen and see how you communicated with the TO. In the middle of that sentence, after saying they were taken to the settlement of Blagaj, the sentence continues, next sentence continues: "The Crisis Staff reacted briskly and issued the order to the TO municipal staff." Not asked them to do something. Ordered them to do something. Is that correct? Is it -- is that correctly translated from the original language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This language and the word "order" is very frequently misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And even if it stands on paper the way it does --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please, please, sir, just answer my question. Is this correctly interpreted? Can you read the corresponding B/C/S language? Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I haven't read it. Then you may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I could judge better how much of the first session tomorrow I'd need if I could have just one more question today, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you, as I did at the beginning, simply to say yes or no whether you agree with me about the following proposition, and perhaps either Mr. Lukic or I will ask you about it in more detail tomorrow. But these people who had been gathered in Blagaj, several thousand Muslims, in fact, several thousand of them were, shortly after the 8th of June when you communicated -- the Crisis Staff communicated that it couldn't guarantee their safety, loaded onto a railway train made up of 22 closed wagons, about 4.000 people were put on it, they were boarded for transportation to Central Bosnia, and that operation was run by Radislav Sekulic, the Chief of Staff of the TO. Do we agree on that point, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know the number. But it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That will enable me to be much more efficient tomorrow, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, we have come to the end of the day for today. We have not finished with your testimony. You'll have to come back tomorrow at 9.30 in the morning so that we can complete your testimony. Before you leave, I would like to warn you that you may not talk to anybody or communicate with anybody in whatsoever about the testimony that you have given today or the testimony that you still have to give tomorrow. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We stand adjourned and we'll resume tomorrow, on the 4th of February, 2015, at 9.30 in the morning, in the same courtroom, I. Court adjourned.
